correctness.rationale: The proof establishes both inclusions for each complete output-language equality for every n≥1. At equal phase, each even-height transition uniquely determines its block; a load-balancing allocation assigns the blocks into exactly n pairs per stream. At opposite phase, the two synchronization states yield independent boundary bits and an attainable complete integer interval containing n, so every block string is realizable. The exact intersection and counting statements follow. Standalone brute mask enumeration matched independent descriptions for n=1..5. Finite checks are supplementary only.

value.rationale: A complete infinite classification of distinct fixed-source shuffle outputs resolves a natural ambiguity phenomenon without identifying outputs with masks. The same length and same Parikh vectors give opposite phases with output-set sizes differing by exactly a factor of two and only one common word. Constructive membership witnesses and the tie between path strips and synchronization states offer reusable structure for restricted shuffle languages. This is not a generic binomial coefficient enumeration or an arbitrary isolated parameter.
